chunks: And in the narration of Ibrāhīm ibn Abī al-Bilād, from someone who mentioned it, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, he said:

During the time of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, there was a truthful woman known as Umm Fattān. A man from the companions of ʿAlī عليه السلام came to her and greeted her, and found her distressed. He said to her, 'Why do I see you distressed?' She said, 'A bondwoman of mine—I buried her, but the earth cast her out twice.' He said: 'So I went in to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and informed him, and he said:'

Indeed, the earth accepts the Jew and the Christian, so there is no reason for this except that she is being punished with the punishment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.' Then he said, 'Indeed, if some soil were taken from the grave of a Muslim man and cast upon her grave, it would settle.'

He said: So I went to Umm Fattān and informed her. She took some soil from the grave of a Muslim man and it was cast upon her grave, and it settled. Then I asked about what she used to do, and they said: 'She was intensely attached to men, and whenever she gave birth, she would throw her child into the oven.'

key_terms.التَّنُّورِ: An oven or furnace, into which she would throw her child.
key_terms.الْأَرْضُ: The earth, described here as accepting or casting out the buried body.
key_terms.تُرْبَةٌ مِنْ قَبْرِ رَجُلٍ مُسْلِمٍ: Soil taken from the grave of a Muslim man, mentioned here as being cast onto the woman's grave.
key_terms.شَدِيدَةَ الْحُبِّ لِلرِّجَالِ: Having an intense attachment to men; a description of her immoral conduct.
key_terms.عَذَابِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: The punishment of Allah, referring here to divine chastisement affecting the deceased.
key_terms.وَلَدَهَا: Her child, referring to the infants she gave birth to.

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about punishment in the grave and the consequences of killing children?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an incident from the time of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام in which a woman's grave was repeatedly rejected by the earth, indicating divine punishment after death. The report links this to her grave sins, especially killing her children, and reflects moral accountability and the reality of punishment connected to one's deeds.
